chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Hashim said: He narrated to us Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman from al-Hasan ibn Ali from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about a man in the countryside who is unable to provide the fitrah (of wheat), so he said: 'He should give charity of four artals of milk.'

key_terms.أَرْطَالٍ: Artals, a unit of weight or volume used in classical Islamic jurisprudence for measuring the fitrah.
key_terms.اللَّبَنِ: Milk, specified here as the alternative commodity for the fitrah.
key_terms.الْبَادِيَةِ: The countryside or rural area, implying a context where specific agricultural products like milk might be more accessible than grain.
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: Fitrah, the alms-tax given at the end of Ramadan, typically in the form of wheat or barley.

ai.seo_question: What is the alternative fitrah for someone who cannot afford or access wheat?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkham outlines the legal ruling for the fitrah (alms-tax) for a person in a rural area who cannot provide the standard wheat. The Imam prescribes that such a person should give charity in the form of four artals of milk instead, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (taysir) and the flexibility of substituting local staples for the canonical grain. This ruling underscores the practical adaptability of fiqh to economic and geographical realities, ensuring the poor are not burdened by unattainable obligations.
